title: What risk costs
how_war_risk_works: Quoted as a percentage of the insured hull value, usually for a seven-day cover period rather than per voyage or per year. Underwriters price individually, so a published rate is indicative. Discounts are common and vessels with US, UK or Israeli links have been quoted materially higher than the market rate.

conflict.field: Strait of Hormuz war risk, July 2026
conflict.previously_contradicted_by: A Reuters reading of 0.5% on 2025-06-23, and the fact that the highest Red Sea figure found anywhere was 2%.
conflict.assessment: RESOLVED 2026-09-06, against the library's own earlier assessment. The 7.5-10% figure is correct and correctly scaled. S&P Global Platts, citing Marsh, published it for 22 July 2026; Lloyd's List corroborated it on 27 July with 'Hormuz war risk cover tops $10m for single VLCC trip'. The error was comparing a July 2026 wartime rate against a June 2025 peacetime one. A US-Israel-Iran war began on 28 February 2026 and Hormuz was effectively closed; the rate moved from 0.1-0.15% before the war to about 2.5% in March and 7.5-10% by late July. For scale, Kharg Island reached 7.5% in May 1984 and Odesa 5% in 2022.
conflict.action: Confidence restored to high and the figure date-stamped. The full dated series is held in insurance-market.json.
conflict.residual_doubt: The library's own 0.5% entry for 2025-06-23 is retained and still attributed to Reuters, but a re-search could not reproduce it; Marsh via Platts gives 0.2% for the Persian Gulf on 19 June 2025, and 0.7% was an Israeli-ports rate. Both readings are kept. Neither affects the July 2026 figure.
